findings: Original handler accepts actual JPEG multipart request whose context is already cancelled, registers background search and emits completion. Tiny empty-directory control, not a transport or latency benchmark.
Original search endpoint tests assert searchId and successful status but do not consume actual matches or verify threshold/workers/topN semantics. Custom parameters test uses empty directory.

Original disconnect test asserts removal from search map but discards search context, so does not assert producer cancellation. SSE success uses manually populated channel rather than live search integration.
Original ServerClose tests assert only nil error with and without cache, no active state or shutdown behavior. This explains why prior lifecycle counterexample coexists with green suite.

Cache hit-rate-named test asserts two misses only, not computed hit rate. Cache-clear-success test clears empty database, not populated state. Cache-scan success asserts SSE and done:true, not cached count or persistence.
Thumbnail success checks JPEG magic, not decoded dimensions or pixel orientation. EXIF endpoint test checks dimensions keys exist rather than numerical correctness.
Most endpoint tests invoke handlers through httptest recorder; passing tests do not qualify actual network transport, browser UI, concurrent consumers or deployment lifecycle.
limits: No fresh full-suite claim: original 72-test record is separate from this new control.
